no prior medical history
alert (GCS 15), afebrile, and appeared well

concepts.why: The combination of bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, superior and lateral semicircular canals, and the right external auditory canal, along with adenoid hypertrophy and mild sinus mucosal thickening, and profound right-sided hearing loss, is consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

The presence of polypoid tissue and purulent secretion in the right external canal, along with a history of otitis media with effusion and tympanic perforation, and bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, suggests a possible cholesteatoma.

The significant difference in hearing thresholds between the left and right ears, with normal wave latencies on the left and prolonged wave I latency on the right, could be indicative of otosclerosis.
